description: Realtime audio framework layer — Vite + WebAudio mic capture, FFT bar visualizer, and a WebRTC peer stub with a documented signalling seam.

buildHints.whenToUse: Pick realtime-audio-ts when the app captures microphone audio in the browser, visualizes it with an AnalyserNode/FFT, and optionally streams audio to a peer via WebRTC. Signalling transport (WebSocket, Ably, Pusher) is intentionally left as a seam.
firstSteps: Run `pnpm install` then `pnpm dev` — Vite serves on 5173; click 'Start microphone' to unlock the AudioContext and see the FFT bars animate.
Audio pipeline lives in src/audio.ts (AudioContext + GainNode + AnalyserNode); the visualizer reads from the analyser in src/visualizer.ts each RAF tick.

WebRTC harness is in src/peer.ts — `createPeer({ stream, onStateChange })` wires tracks and exposes createOffer/acceptAnswer; add your own WebSocket transport where the SIGNALLING TODO comments appear.
Run `pnpm build` to emit static assets to dist/ — no server required, deploy to any static host.
gotchas: AUTOPLAY POLICY: call audioContext.resume() inside the Start button click handler — creating an AudioContext at module load leaves it suspended and getByteFrequencyData returns all zeros with no error.
getUserMedia requires HTTPS or localhost. Use `vite --host --https` for LAN device testing.
Preallocate the Uint8Array for getByteFrequencyData ONCE at attach() time and reuse every RAF frame — allocating inside the loop causes GC jank at 60fps.
Call pc.addTrack() for every stream track BEFORE pc.createOffer(), otherwise the SDP lacks an m=audio line and the remote peer has nothing to answer.
iOS Safari destroys the AudioContext after 30s in background — listen to visibilitychange and call context.resume() on return.
architectureNotes: src/audio.ts owns the AudioContext lifecycle — created in the constructor, resumed in unlock() which must be called from within a user-gesture handler.
src/visualizer.ts drives rendering from requestAnimationFrame; the buffer is preallocated at attach() time to avoid GC pressure in the hot loop.
src/peer.ts is a WebRTC harness: call createPeer({ stream, onStateChange }) after getUserMedia, then createOffer() when ready to initiate. Signalling transport is intentionally left as a seam.

placeholders.description: SIGNALLING TODO comments mark exactly where to wire a WebSocket, Ably, Pusher, or socket.io transport for ICE candidate exchange.
